questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction $2 \mathrm{SO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{SO}_3$, the rate of disappearance of $\mathrm{O}_2$ is $2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{ mol} \mathrm{ L}^{-1}\mathrms^{-1}$. The rate appearance of $\mathrm{SO}_3$ is
questions.solution:
$2 \mathrm{SO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{SO}_3$
Rate of reaction $=-\frac{1}{2} \frac{d\left[\mathrm{SO}_2\right]}{d t}=-\frac{d\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{1}{2} \frac{d\left[\mathrm{SO}_3\right]}{d t}$
Rate of appearance of $\mathrm{SO}_3$,
$\begin{aligned}
\frac{d\left[\mathrm{SO}_3\right]}{d t} & =2 \times\left[\frac{-d\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]}{d t}\right]=2 \times\left(2 \times 10^{-4}\right) \\
& =4 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{ mol} \mathrm{ L}^{-1} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
If for a first order reaction, the value of $A$ and $E_a$ are $4 \times 10^{13} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$ and $98.6 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$
respectively, then at what temperature will its half life period be 10 minutes?
questions.solution:
According to Arrhenius equation,
$\log k=\log A-\frac{E_a}{2.303 R T}...(i)$
For $1^{\text{st }}$ order reaction,
$k=\frac{0.693}{t_{1 / 2}}=\frac{0.693}{600 s}=1.1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$
Substitute the value of $k$ in Eq. (i)
$\log \left(1.1 \times 10^{-3}\right)=\log \left(4 \times 10^{13}\right)-\frac{98.6 \times 10^3}{2.303 \times 8.314 \times T}$
Solving for $T$,
$T=311.15 \mathrm{ K}$

questions.q: In the chemical reaction $A \rightarrow B$, what is the order of the reaction? Given that, the rate of reaction doubles if the concentration of $A$ is increased four times.
questions.solution:
We know, $r_1=k[A]^{\mathrm{n}}$....(i)
If conc. of $A$ is increased four times rate of reaction on doubles.
$2 r_1=k[4 A]^{\mathrm{n}}$....(ii) Divide Eq. (ii) by (i).
$\frac{2 r_i}{r_1}=\frac{k(4 A)^n}{k(A)^n}\Rightarrow \quad 2=(4)^{\mathrm{n}} \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{n}=(2)^{2 \mathrm{n}} \Rightarrow n=0.5$

questions.q: $\mathrm{XmL}$ of $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ gas effuses through a hole in a container in 5 seconds. The time taken for the effusion of the same volume of the gas specified below under identical conditions is :
questions.solution:
Under identical conditions, $ rac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}=\sqrt{ rac{\mathrm{M}_{2}}{\mathrm{M}_{1}}}$ As rate of diffusion is also inversely proportional to time, we will have, $ rac{t_{2}}{t_{1}}=\sqrt{ rac{\overline{\mathrm{M}_{2}}}{\mathrm{M}_{1}}}$ (A) Thus, For $\mathrm{He}, t_{2}=\sqrt{ rac{4}{2}}(5 s)=5 \sqrt{2} s 
eq 10 s$; (B) $\mathrm{For} \mathrm{O}_{2}, t_{2}=\sqrt{ rac{32}{2}}(5 s)=20 s$ (C) For $\mathrm{CO}, t_{2}=\sqrt{ rac{28}{2}}(5 s) 
eq 25 s$; (D) For $\mathrm{CO}_{2}, t_{2}=\sqrt{ rac{44}{2}}(5 s) 
eq 55 s$ #

questions.q:
Which of the following expression is correct for the rate of reaction given below ?

$5{Br}^{-} \left(aq\right) + {BrO}_{3}^{-} \left(aq\right) + 6H^{+} \left(aq\right) ⟶ 3{Br}_{2}\left(aq\right)$+ $3{H}_{2}O \left(l\right)$
questions.solution:
The given chemical reaction is

$5{Br}^{-}\left(aq\right) + {BrO}_{3}^{-} \left(aq\right) + 6H^{+} \left(aq\right) ⟶ 3{Br}_{2}\left(aq\right) + 3{H}_{2}O\left(l\right)$

Rate law expression for the given reaction can be written as

$- \dfrac{1}{5}\dfrac{\Delta\left[{Br}^{-}\right]}{Δt} = - \dfrac{\Delta\left[{BrO}_{3}^{-}\right]}{Δt}$

$- \dfrac{1}{6}\dfrac{\Delta\left[H^{+}\right]}{Δt} = + \dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{\Delta\left[{Br}_{2}\right]}{Δt}$

$⇒ - \dfrac{\Delta\left[{Br}^{-}\right]}{Δt} = - \dfrac{5\Delta\left[{BrO}_{3}^{-}\right]}{Δt} = - \dfrac{5}{6}\dfrac{\Delta\left[H^{+}\right]}{Δt}$

$\dfrac{\Delta\left[{Br}^{-}\right]}{Δt} = \dfrac{5}{6}\dfrac{\Delta\left[H^{+}\right]}{Δt}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For an endothermic reaction, where $\Delta H$ represent the enthalpy of reaction in $kJ{mol}^{- 1}$, the minimum value for energy of activation (for forward reaction) will be
questions.solution:
We know that, $\Delta H = {E}_{f} - {E}_{b}$

where, ${E}_{b}$ and ${E}_{f} =$ activation energy for backward and forward respectively.

Thus,${E}_{f} = \Delta H + {E}_{b}$, means ${E}_{f} > \Delta H$.

$\Delta H =$ heat of reaction (endothermic)

${E}_{a} =$ energy of activation

Thus, ${E}_{a} > \Delta H$

Heat is absorbed in an endothermic reaction. Thus, for an endothermic reaction, where $\Delta H$ represent the enthalpy of reaction in $kJ{mol}^{- 1}$, the minimum value for energy of activation (for forward reaction) will be more than $\Delta H$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction, $\mathrm{P}+\mathrm{Q} \longrightarrow ? \mathrm{R}+\mathrm{S}$ The time taken for $75 \%$ reaction of $P$ is twice the time taken for $50 \%$ reaction of $\mathrm{P}$. The concentration of $\mathrm{Q}$ varies with reaction time as shown in the figure. The overall order of the reaction is
questions.solution: For $\mathrm{P}$, if $\mathrm{t}_{50 \%}=\mathrm{x}$ then $\mathrm{t}_{75 \%}=2 \mathrm{x}$ This is true only for first order reaction. So, order with respect to $\mathrm{P}$ is $1.$ Further the graph shows that concentration of $\mathrm{Q}$ decreases with time. So rate, with respect to $\mathrm{Q},$ remains constant. Hence, it is zero order wrt Q. So, overall order is $1+0=1$
